answer.question: What should I have ready for a Highlands Ranch turf estimate?
answer.answer: Bring your intended use, property plan and current HRCA or other applicable community requirements. Show us the access route, existing irrigation, wet areas and any soils information you have. Those details help define the layout and any preparation decisions still needed.

blocks.h2: Look at when you will use the yard.
paras: An established yard with mature trees and a newer open yard need different conversations about placement. For pets or family use, consider the time spent in full sun and room for shade. Turf can become hot; choose the position with that use in mind.
A putting green needs useful lines and walking room, not simply the sunniest patch. Decide which distances to practice and how the green will sit beside the patio or planting.

Use the applicable Highlands Ranch community guidelines for your property and proposed change. Include turf boundaries, edges and the landscape that will remain when asking what needs to be submitted. Keep any required response separate from the installation estimate.

If you are comparing water costs, use your provider’s current information and your own bills. Confirm incentive eligibility directly; a lawn-replacement program does not necessarily fund synthetic turf.

blocks.h2: Odd addresses water Wednesday and Saturday. Even, Thursday and Sunday.
paras: Highlands Ranch Water, run by Centennial Water and Sanitation District, is in Stage 1 drought as of 3 September 2026, aiming to cut use by 15 to 20% (Highlands Ranch Water). Homes get two watering days, picked by house number: odd on Wednesday and Saturday, even on Thursday and Sunday, apartments on Monday and Friday and businesses on Tuesday and Sunday, with no watering from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Hand-watering and drip are allowed any time.

Fines climb with each violation after a warning: $50, $100, $250, then $500 by the fifth. Water above your account's budget costs more as well; at 101 to 120% of budget, the residential rate goes from $7.66 to $9.58.
Turf takes that ground out of the schedule, the budget and the fine ladder all at once.

blocks.h2: Half the front yard, two feet off every line, 1.5-inch pile.
paras: Highlands Ranch homes sit under the Highlands Ranch Community Association, and most exterior improvements need the Architecture Committee's written approval before work starts (HRCA). Turf is reviewed case by case, and the submittal needs a sample of the material and a drainage plan alongside the landscape plan.

The written spec is short and firm. Synthetic turf must not exceed 50% of the area in the front yard, must stay a minimum of two feet from all property lines, must be a minimum 1.5-inch pile with straw-colored thatch, and must be ASTM certified material. Side and rear yards may be considered at 100% coverage, judged on how they look from neighboring properties, the screening and planting around them, and the landscape plan as a whole (Residential Improvement Guidelines, adopted October 2024 and updated June 2025).

The committee or staff has 30 days to answer once it holds everything it asked for, so put that in your dates. On a detached lot the association can shape back-yard turf but can't forbid it (SB23-178); the front yard stays its call, inside that 50%.

blocks.h2: Against a parkway fence, the last foot inside it isn't yours.
paras: The Metro District owns more than 42 miles of parkway fence along the arterials, from Wildcat Reserve and Fairview to University and South Broadway, and where that fence runs beside a back yard the District owns or holds easements for the land 12 inches inside the fence line. Its rules stop you setting landscape material against the fence, and it asks for a 12-inch buffer (Highlands Ranch Metro District). Add HRCA's two-foot setback and the turf on those lots stops well short of the fence, with planting or rock filling the gap. Check the District's street list for your road, and we measure the real edge before the layout is drawn.

The open space behind you is not a way in. HRCA answers that one plainly: the Metro District owns and maintains the majority of open spaces and prohibits using the open space to install any home improvement (HRCA). The District's land use rules also bar storage or staging of equipment or materials, and dumping of sod, soil or landscape materials, on its ground (land use rules). Pallets, base rock and the old lawn all come and go through the side yard or the drive, so show us that route.

Underneath is Douglas County's swelling clay, which the Colorado Geological Survey flags across the county (Colorado Geological Survey). Have your soils report out at the free visit; base depth, compaction and drainage all follow the ground it describes. Erosion running off your yard onto Metro District land is on their prohibited list too, so the drainage has to keep the water on your side.

faq.q: Who installs artificial turf in Highlands Ranch, CO?
faq.a: We install artificial turf, pet turf and backyard putting greens in Highlands Ranch, CO. As of 3 September 2026, Highlands Ranch Water is in Stage 1: odd addresses water Wednesday and Saturday, even addresses Thursday and Sunday, never from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., with fines up to $500. Centennial Water no longer rebates artificial turf. Call 303-349-2368 for a free estimate.

faq.q: What does HRCA require before artificial turf goes in?
faq.a: Written approval, and turf that meets four specifics: no more than 50% of the front yard, a minimum of two feet from all property lines, a minimum 1.5-inch pile with straw-colored thatch, and ASTM certified material. Side and rear yards may be considered at 100% coverage (Residential Improvement Guidelines). Send a material sample and a drainage plan with the landscape plan, and ask the Community Improvement Services department what the current review fee is, because the guidelines don't publish one.

faq.q: Will the water rebate pay for artificial turf?
faq.a: No. Artificial turf replacements are no longer eligible, and every landscape conversion has to be approved by HRCA, or by the Solstice Architectural Control Committee, before it begins (Highlands Ranch Water). The rebate reopens on 1 March 2027 and pays $2.50 a square foot for ColoradoScape and $1.50 for low-water turf grasses such as Dog Tuff and Tahoma 31. Resource Central's lawn program, which Highlands Ranch Water partners with, needs half the new area in waterwise plants and has closed for 2026 (Resource Central).

faq.q: Can HOAs and schools in Highlands Ranch put in artificial turf?
faq.a: Under Stage 1, HOAs, government and schools are asked to cut water use by 15 to 20% (Highlands Ranch Water). State law now keeps new non-functional turf out of HOA common areas such as entry monuments and medians, but ball fields are left out (SB24-005).

faq.q: Can the crew work off the open space behind my house?
faq.a: No. The Metro District owns and maintains most of the open space and prohibits using it to install any home improvement (HRCA). Its land use rules also bar storage or staging of materials and dumping of sod or soil on District ground (land use rules). The way in is your side yard or your drive, and we check that route on the free visit.

faq.q: Which Highlands Ranch yards suit a putting green?
faq.a: The sunnier south-end yards from the 2000s have the room and the light for one. Under north-end trees, a green fits where the canopy leaves an opening, and either way it sits on the same clay-ready base as the lawn.
